newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rebound from Friday slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rebound from Friday slide.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures staged a rebound from Friday's steep losses, and most contracts ended sharply higher.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures surged toward the 920.00 handle in afternoon trade as bargain buyers emerged amid sentiment that Friday's losses were overdone.
On Friday, September stumbled to a 6-1/2-week low and the bellwether Dow posted its largest one-day point loss since the October 1987 crash.
Technicians said Monday's late rally helped soothe at least some of the market's oversold status from Friday.
Paul Hare, a technician with LIT's The Linn Group, said Friday's break completed a 50 percent retracement of the May 30 to August 7 rally, prompting reversal action Monday.
"Not only did we complete a retracement but we came up against the June support at the 880.00 to 890.00 area," Hare said, allowing the market to bounce sharply Monday.

September S&P 500s started the session firm after recovering on GLOBEX overnight trade, but faltered near midday and tested downside territory. In early afternoon, September crawled higher and it rallied strongly after debt futures closed.
Still, traders said the day's volume was only light to moderate.
On Monday, September traded an estimated 63,000 contracts, as shown on trading floor price boards. On Friday, September traded 69,308 contracts.
A few traders said Monday's estimate may be overstated, and said the lighter volume on the higher day could be a warning sign.
"We hit a few stops at 915.00 that brought us to the highs, but it was basically on thin volume," a trader said. "I think tomorrow there could be a nice little selloff."
A Federal Open Market Committee meeting Tuesday was expected to yield no change in official U.S. interest rates, but traders said the meeting could keep players nervous.
"It should make for an interesting day tomorrow," another trader said.
Several traders noted good buying at 896.00 near midday.

At the close, Sept S&P 500s rose 19.95 to 918.75, Russell 2000 was up 1.60 at 412.10, Value Lines rose 8.90 pts to 830.90, NYSE Composite rose 9.15 to 476.75, NASDAQ rose 23.75 to 1096.25, and Nikkei rose 185.0 to 19,215.00.
